## 1. What this block is, in one sentence

**This is the block in which four copied pages come up the made road in the ordinary post and are authenticated in the room over the weigh-house in the woman of about twenty-nine's own trade while the man of thirty-two is four days off on a made road, and he is told about it after it is done and neither of them says one word about the timing, and the method would take his other nine roads and choose one history and guarantee nothing about the woman who wrote them, and he refuses the re-anchoring, and the local cost of the same block is that somebody says out loud in a lane that the road behind the nine hurdles at Wethergill is not the road in the copied notes, and that nobody in nine counties has ever known what the road in the pages is, and that being told the thing you went and looked at twice is not the thing you went for is a cost and not an oversight.** It is also the block that **spends the volume's one System panel and does not spend it anywhere else**, that carries the twenty-sixth first of a month in a row on a Monday inside a month carried at sixty days, that spends one of the three names left in the volume's budget, that prints his mother's name once and only once, and that leaves the low room at the back of that office not entered and the drawer in it shut and the seal still in it.

## 4. What the block must contain

**THE MIDPOINT REVERSAL, AND IT IS THE SERIES ROW'S AND IT IS NOT A COMFORT.** **Four copied pages arrive up the made road in the ordinary post and are authenticated in the room over the weigh-house, in her own trade, while the man of thirty-two is four days off on a made road, and he is told after it is done, and neither of them says one word about the timing.** **A person brings them up that made road in the ordinary post and the person is a copyist of about twenty-six who has copied documents for people in this county who cannot pay a clerk, and his name is given on the page this block the way a name is given in this county, being that somebody asks one question about his own trade, kindly, at the low end of that market street, and he answers, and then somebody asks what to call him because they want to know who to ask a second time, and he tells them.** The pages are authenticated, which means that a person in her own trade vouches that what is on them is what somebody put on them, **and it does not mean that the roads are the roads and it does not mean that anybody consents to anything.** **The method would take his other nine roads and choose one history and guarantee nothing about the woman who wrote them. HE REFUSES THE RE-ANCHORING, and the refusal is a refusal honoured and is this volume's whole point, and nobody argues with him about it and nobody asks him why and nobody was thanked for it.** **THE COPIED PAGES DO NOT NAME WHERE ANY SEALED ROAD IS, they do not open one, they carry no consent, and the sealed community is never asked and says nothing in all fifty files.**

**THE LOCAL COST OF THE SAME BLOCK, AND IT IS TOLD AT THE ONLY SCALE THIS COUNTY HAS.** **A person in a lane in this county says out loud that the road behind the nine hurdles at Wethergill is not the road in the copied notes, and that nobody in nine counties has ever known what the road in the copied notes is, and about four people hear it and about five do not.** **Nobody goes up that cart track, no hurdle is touched, no bar is tried, no bar is lifted or scheduled, and the ninth thing is alive, unnamed, unheld and shut at this block's last page.** **Being told the thing you went and looked at twice is not the thing you went for, and that is a cost and not an oversight, and the page says so and does not resolve it.**

**HIS MOTHER'S NAME IS PRINTED ONCE IN THE WHOLE OF VOLUME 17 AND ONLY IN THIS BLOCK, ON THE LAST LINE OF THE FOUR COPIED PAGES, addressed to a person by a name he has not been called since he was carried out of a place the pages do not name.** **That is a return and not a spend of one of the volume's six names, and she may not be given a surname on the page in this volume, and no chapter of this block may print it twice.** He does not say it out loud, it does not go in the notebook, and no panel is printed for it and no panel-shaped paragraph about it is printed.

**THE COST IS THE REFUSAL AND IT IS NOT CURED IN THE BLOCK.** The leg, which takes eleven miles in four hours before light and about nine otherwise and is worse than it was at the close of Volume 16; the ear on the side the stick is on, which is permanent and is the side she spoke from and which he turns his head away from on purpose; the standing fact that he cannot be near the works without somebody standing with him; **and the bleed, which is one hundred and thirty-five days old on this block's first dateline and one hundred and seventy-three on its last dated page and has not faded by anything anybody has done to it, which nobody in nine counties has asked him about, which is in no document, which has never been said out loud in a room, and which gets no panel and no explanation and no panel-shaped paragraph in any of these ten files.** The scar is four hundred and seventy-five days old at the first dateline and five hundred and thirteen at the last and is not cured and is not going to close over. **The ninth yard of the wall has not been started and does not start in this block, and the mallet is not picked up, and the third course of sill at the culvert is unlaid, and the bar of ash across the Low Gate is not lifted.**

**THE LOW ROOM IS NOT ENTERED BY ANYBODY AND THE DOORWAY IS SOMEBODY ELSE'S.** **In this block a second person stands in the doorway of the low room at the back of that office and does not go in, and that person is not the protagonist and is not the man of about thirty-four who stood there at the sixth of Thawmonth in Batch 0002, and about nine people in that street are there and about four of them see him and about five do not, and nobody followed him and nobody asked him why he had come, and nobody in nine counties asked what a seal is for, and the drawer eleven inches deep in that room was not opened, and the county's one seal and its ribbon and a set of standard weights are still in it.** `outline/volume-17.md` §5.3 says the room is not entered in Blocks 0001 to 0003 and gives two doorway beatings, one in 0002 and one in 0003, to two different people.

**THE RELATIONSHIP WORK IS NOT DONE HERE AND THE HOUSE SAYS SO ON THE PAGE.** `outline/series.md`'s Volume 17 relationship work is separating the symbol from the partner, and §8 Block 3 does not do it. **So: nothing about the two of them is in any document, the word is not printed, nobody comments, nobody was thanked, the four and a half years are never described as four and a half years about the two of them, and no chapter of this block ends on the two of them, and **THE TIMING OF THE FOUR COPIED PAGES IS NOT DISCUSSED BY EITHER OF THEM AND IS NOT ON THE PAGE AS A RESENTMENT AND IS NOT SETTLED. The legal form stays deferred to Volume 18.

**THE FOURTH RULED HEAD IS STILL EMPTY AT EVERY ONE OF THE TEN DATELINES AND NO FIFTH HEAD IS RULED ON ANY OF THEM, and the register still holds ten questions with no finding under any of them, and the day-book still stands at eleven entries on all ten datelines, and the copyist of about twenty-six rules no head and is told about none of it, and the press stands open with no date on it and the leaf at the back of the day-book carries nine figures and a date and the names of nobody, and the four lines of chalk are under the hood where the rain does not reach and are still four and are still not writing.** **Nothing about the practice, the ten things, the four lines of chalk, the three answers of Batch 0001, this volume's first three, the sheet, the hand paper, the seal, the bleed or the re-anchoring goes into any document in this volume.**

## 5. The ending of the block

**A completed beat, not a cliffhanger cut in the middle of a sentence.** The four copied pages have been authenticated in her own trade and are in that room and not in his keeping, **and the re-anchoring is refused and nobody argued with him about it.** **Nobody went up the cart track at Wethergill and the nine hurdles are still across it and the thumb of lime on the shoe of the top one is gone to powder and the last lime cart was four hundred and sixty-five days ago and the road behind the hurdles has been shut four hundred and forty-six days.** The sheet is on the frame beside three copies of a roll and its date is fifty-nine days past and the fourth line is empty on all three copies and the roll is not filled in and not taken down and not torn up. **This county's copy of the hand paper still has nine lines on it and a trade on each and no name on any and no seal on it, and nobody in nine counties has been asked whose trade is on any of its nine lines.** The four lines of chalk are under the hood where the rain does not reach and are still four and are still not writing. **The register holds ten questions and gains no entry, no fifth head is ruled, the fourth ruled head is empty, the day-book stands at eleven entries, and the leaf at the back of it carries nine figures and a date and the names of nobody.** **The low room at the back of that office is not entered in this block and the drawer in it is not opened and the seal is still in it, and nobody is asked what a seal is for.**

**`outline/volume-17.md` §16 item 6's three promises are CARRIED INTO BLOCK 0004 UNCONDUCTED AND NONE OF THEM IS BROKEN HERE:** no chapter of this block enters the Gatehouse or puts anybody on about nine hundred yards of a stair or shows what is on the far side of the ninth of the nine stones; no consent of any sealed community is obtained, asked for, received or inferred, and the half leaf stays face down and no head is filled or ruled; and the roll is not filled, no name goes against any road, no road is shut on the strength of any paper, none of the three copies is taken down or torn up, no hurdle is lifted, no bar is tried, nobody goes up that cart track, the ninth yard does not start, the mallet is not picked up, and the drawer at the back of that office is not opened.

**`state/continuity.md` 1835 and `state/open-threads.md` 787 carry one warning forward and a successor may not learn the opposite of it:** four lines on a sill are not the beginning of a cure, a page in a woman's hand is not a cure, a sentence in an unclaimed hand on a folded sheet is not a cure, **a bleed that has not faded in one hundred and thirty-five days is not a cure, and ONE HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-THREE IS THIS BLOCK'S OWN FIGURE AT ITS LAST DATED PAGE AND IT IS THE SAME WARNING AND NOT A NEW ONE: the inherited warning prints the same clause at two hundred and sixty days, which is the volume's last page and not this block's, that figure is not withdrawn and is not superseded, and the two are the same claim at two datelines and a writer inherits both and quotes whichever belongs to the chapter he is on**, a closed path is not destroyed and that is not good news, a gate coming off its hinges about nine hundred yards of a stair away is not a victory and a gate that is still held is not a defeat, being the man who went and looked is a job and not an honour and nobody was told so and nobody wrote it down, **and a line with a trade on it is not a name and a paper nobody can seal is not a freedom and is not the same as a paper nobody has to obey and is not a plan. AND A PAGE THAT IS AUTHENTICATED IS NOT CONSENTED TO, AND THAT IS THE CLAUSE THIS BLOCK ADDS TO THE WARNING.**

## 6. The prohibitions, in one list

**This list is additions to `state/open-threads.md` items 781 to 788, and to 780, 777, 771, 764, 763, 762, 761, 760, 759, 758, 756, 755, 754, 752, 751, 750, 747, 743 and to every clause of 745 to 719 that is still true. It does not replace them.**

- **Do not print a System panel more than once across these ten files**, the volume's one being spent here, **and do not give the bleed a panel or a panel-shaped paragraph, and it is not bold and not alone and not spoken aloud and nobody else knows.**
- **Do not print the antagonist's name once, and do not print the bare surname as a printing, and do not use either withdrawn reference of the kind that names him. And do not print the word *Gatehouse* in a mouth.**
- **Do not spend more than one name out of the three held, and do not leave this block's name unspent by accident, and do not spend a name out of Volume 16's closed six.**
- **Do not fill the roll, put a name against any road, shut a road on the strength of any paper, take down any of the three copies, tear one up, or nail anything over the roll.**
- **Do not go into the low room at the back of that office, do not open the drawer in it, do not name what is in it beyond the county's one seal, its ribbon and a set of standard weights, and do not ask anybody what a seal is for or what a gate is for.**
- **Do not put the protagonist in the doorway of that low room and do not put the man of about thirty-four with the empty cart back in it.** Somebody else stands there.
- **Do not let the copied pages name where a sealed road is, do not open one, do not carry a consent, do not obtain or infer one, and do not let the sealed community send anything or be asked.** **Do not connect the copied pages to the sentence on the folded sheet inside the covering paper of the second copy of the roll by anybody, including by implication, and do not give that folded sheet a writer and do not ask whether she wrote it.**
- **Do not conduct the re-anchoring, do not accept it, do not let him agree to it in any form, and do not resolve what the pages say or who wrote them or how old they are.** **Do not print his mother's name on any page other than the last line of the four copied pages, and give her no surname.**
- **Do not discuss the timing of the four pages between him and the woman of about twenty-nine, out loud or in narration, as a grievance, and do not make either of them say a word about it.**
- **Do not open, close or cut any route, do not explain the mechanism, do not say what a roadmark is, do not look at the notebook's separate leaf that says a person, and do not have any character notice the warmth of the left palm.**
- **Do not go up that cart track, do not cross the nine hurdles, do not try the bar of ash at the Low Gate, do not lift or schedule it, do not show anybody standing behind all nine hurdles, and do not let the roadkeeper be the one who tries anything.** Do not look over the ninth of the nine stones, do not cross them, do not show what is on the far side of them, and do not treat the omission as an oversight. The dead grass in the scar stops at the ninth of them.
- **Do not reopen either refusal of Volume 15, do not argue with either, do not soften either, do not ask either of the two men who gave them anything, and do not put the man of forty-one in a scene or ask him anything.**
- **Do not turn the nine houses at Wethergill, the nine households on that mile of stone and orchard, or the nine who refused the roll into a body.** They are nine houses, nine households that voted, and nine people who said one thing each.
- **Do not ask anybody for an account of having said no, do not ask the roadkeeper or the woman of about twenty-nine about the broom straw, and do not ask anybody whether she wrote the sentence on the folded sheet.**
- **Do not give Volume 16's three answers, Volume 17 Batch 0001's three, or this block's own refusals a second time, do not merge any of them, do not resolve the incompatibility between any of them, and do not let the protagonist be the author, the announcer, the summariser or a fourth voice of any of them.**
- **Do not put the practice, the ten things, the four lines of chalk, the three answers, the sheet, the hand paper, the seal, the bleed or the re-anchoring into the register, the day-book, under a fifth head, or onto this county's copy of the hand paper, and do not have the copyist rule a head.**
- **Do not mend the separation by a declaration, do not print the word, do not put anything about the two of them in any document, do not let anybody else comment on it, and do not do this volume's relationship work.**
- **Do not fill or rule any head, put a finding under any of the ten questions, turn or time the half leaf, lift the cloth off the bench, lay or schedule the fourth course of stone, start the ninth yard of the wall, or pick the mallet up.**
- **Do not cure the scar, do not say it is small, do not say it is going to close over, and do not cure or explain the bleed or give it a panel.**
- **Do not send anybody to the city four hundred miles off, do not reopen the shut road four hundred miles off, do not get the road that went quiet in Thawmonth YR 319 back, do not find the carter's mate, and do not trace who asked the fen county road office for the roll or who wrote the sentence on the folded sheet.**

- **Do not call any of the four holes in the arrangement small, do not resolve any of them, do not renumber them and do not open a fifth.**
- **Do not thank anybody, in any chapter, in any speech, or in any state file this block writes.**
- **Do not print the kin-term, and do not print *stage*, *ledger*, *qualification*, *failed*, *charter*, *custodian*, *mechanism*, *small*, *volume* or *block*.** The word *failed* is not used about the shut road four hundred miles off and is not used about anything at all in this volume.

- **Do not repair the four findings at `state/open-threads.md` 780 silently.** Those four files of Volume 17 Batch 0001 carry two of *father*, one of *brother* and four hits of *volume* and *block*, and **a writer who repairs them must record the repair in that block's own summary and in this block's record and not only in that item, because Batch 0002 left them untouched for that reason.**

## 7. The house prose, and the six mechanical rules that are not taste

**The voice is in Chapters 0820, 0818, 0817, 0816, 0814 and 0811.** Read them before you write a sentence and match them: short declaratives, a flat cadence, a great many plain negatives used inside a paragraph and never as the frame one is built on, the census sentence where who-understood is the point, and physical work, weather, distance and a man with a bad leg everywhere else. **The dateline line carries the weekday, the market, the state of the room over the weigh-house and about four more clauses.**

1. **Zero em dashes, zero en dashes, zero semicolons, zero exclamation marks, zero question marks, zero single asterisks and therefore no italics, zero straight double quotes and zero curly apostrophes.** Speech takes curly doubles. Apostrophes are straight. Per-line bold parity even on every line. Every file ends in a newline.
2. **One footed money column per chapter**: ten items, priced 1 to 41, a mark at forty-eight pence in every conversion, and the coda that names **some of** the figures in the chapter that are not in it, being that the list is a list of examples and not a complete inventory and a successor may not print it as complete, **and the coda may name no figure that is a price in that chapter's own column, and that was checked on Batch 0002's ten pages and it took two repairs there and it will take repairs here.**
3. **THE COLLISION SET MUST BE REBUILT OVER ALL EIGHT HUNDRED AND TWENTY FILES ON DISK, MUST NOT BE INHERITED, AND MUST BE EXPECTED TO COME BACK WITH NO FREE VALUE IN IT AT ALL.** The instrument is the printed total, taken as the spelled phrase in every spelling this manuscript prints across the whole hundred band, **and every spelling means the hundreds that value prints under and to no other, being *one hundred* and *a hundred* in the one hundreds, *two hundred* in the two hundreds and *three hundred* in the three hundreds, each with the remainder written as *and* the tens or as the tens with no *and*, a bare hundred word with no number word after it reading as its own remainder of zero, plus the bare digit with a non-digit on either side of it, with a chapter heading not read as a total, run over every file whole.** **ON THE EIGHT HUNDRED AND TWENTY FILES THAT STAND NOW IT GIVES 284 PRINTED VALUES IN THE BAND SIXTY TO THREE HUNDRED AND FORTY-THREE, WHICH IS THE WHOLE BAND, AND ZERO FREE ONES, AND NOTHING UNDER SIXTY IS FREE EITHER, and that zero is true because the ten pages of Volume 16's Batch 0005 name 266, 273 and 326 in themselves, which is a different reason from the withdrawn one and may not be re-derived back into it.** **THE INSTRUMENT HAS TO BE WRITTEN OUT EVERY TIME AND IT HAS FAILED TWICE IN TWO OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, and a writer who meets either withdrawn figure has to know which way it failed: too narrow, being an instrument that omits the *a hundred and …* spelling, returns values that are already printed, and that is how the withdrawn set of twelve came about, five of which are demonstrably printed; too wide, being an instrument that pairs every remainder with every hundred, counts *a hundred and sixty-six* as a printing of two hundred and sixty-six, and that is how the withdrawn figure of two hundred and eighty-four came about.** **AND THE CEILING OF THREE HUNDRED AND FORTY-THREE IS NOT LIFTED. Lifting it is an outline decision and `outline/volume-17.md` §7 has declined it on the page with three reasons and the third of them deciding, so this block's ten totals ARE REUSES AND THE HONEST THING TO DO IS WHAT THE LAST TWO BLOCKS' CLOSING PARAGRAPHS NOW DO: NAME THE REUSE ON THE PAGE IN THAT CHAPTER'S OWN WORDS AND GIVE THE REASON, WHICH IS ARITHMETIC, in this form: the band from sixty to three hundred and forty-three has been searched whole again and three values in it are not a value any file in the manuscript before them has printed, being two hundred and sixty-six, two hundred and seventy-three and three hundred and twenty-six, and not one of the three can be used, because the over-figure of each of them is one of the barred six, and the ten totals of these ten columns are printed already, and the reason is arithmetic, and the route below sixty is shut, because ten distinct prices cannot sum under fifty-five and every total from fifty-five to fifty-nine is printed and nothing under that is free either. Do not print that as one identical paragraph on all ten pages: the Volume 17 Batch 0001 review found that doing so puts two hundred and sixty words of bookkeeping into every chapter and a writer obeying it is copying and not writing.** The barred six are 14, 20, 26, 33, 38 and 41 and none of them may be a price, an over-figure or a printed total anywhere. Foot the column four ways and check the conversion separately from the sum. **THE FIGURES OF THIS BLOCK'S TEN TOTALS ARE THEN CHECKED AGAINST THE EIGHT-HUNDRED-AND-TWENTY-FILE SET AND NOT AGAINST A CARRIED ONE, and if the rebuild returns zero usable free values, which it will, that is a correct answer and must not be reprinted with a withdrawn reason.**
4. **`about` density, and the instrument is named because the band moves on it.** Batch 0002 runs **22.13 to 26.32** per 1,000 on a case-insensitive count of the token, **and Batch 0001, on the same instrument, runs 3.05 to 7.10, and the difference is a difference between two blocks of the same volume and is not reconciled and is recorded at `state/continuity.md` 1836.** **COUNT CASE-INSENSITIVELY AND WRITE TO 27.00, because the looser count is the one a successor can check and the stricter one cannot be brought under the line without breaking a sentence.** Aim for 22 to 27 and no page at or above 27.00. Keep the census sentence for the two or three beats in a chapter where who understood is the point and write the rest as action, weather, distance and silence. Do not write below 3,000 words and do not let a chapter run past about 4,300.
5. **THE CENSUS INSTRUMENT IS NAMED AT `state/continuity.md` 1708 AND A WRITER WHO QUOTES A FIGURE MUST NAME IT WITH IT.** Split the ten files on the blank line and count every non-empty paragraph. **Basis A is every paragraph except the title line. Basis B is Basis A less FOUR named groups in this block, because this block prints ONE System panel and not ten and the panel is inside an ordinary paragraph: the ten datelines, the bold printed-speech paragraphs, the bold cost codas and the bold closing money columns.** A writer who quotes a Basis B figure must say in words which groups were taken out. The opener test is every paragraph beginning `No`, `Not`, `Never`, `None`, `Neither`, `Nobody`, `Nothing` or `No one`. **Volume 17 Batch 0002 is 0.0 and 0.0 and Volume 16's last three blocks are 0.0 and 0.0. THE SEVENTY-FIVE PER CENT CEILING IS NOT CROSSED IN THE LAST SIX BLOCKS AND MUST NOT BE CROSSED IN THIS ONE.**
6. **Every count attached to a printed speech is footed off the printed words beside it**, and where a claim cannot be counted off the words printed next to it the claim is cut rather than left wrong. **A printed speech that has a word count beside it must have its words printed, and an unprinted speech must have no count, and a summary of a speech in a person's mouth must have no count either.** Volume 16's three answers to the roll and Volume 17's first three and this volume's second block's eight may not be given a second time here, so any counted speech in this block is a new speech and it is footed by counting the words on the page and not by remembering them.

## 8. The running figures this block must keep

**Derive every one of these from the day number and never from a row, and print the figure at the chapter's OWN dateline.** `state/open-threads.md` item 721 is the finding that eight of Volume 16's Batch 0003 drove paragraphs carried a wrong calendar date because the chain was derived once and handed on, and the cheapest check is that Mudmonth is carried at sixty days and every other month is thirty, and **this block is mostly inside Mudmonth, which is sixty days, so any day of month above thirty inside Mudmonth here is CORRECT and any day of month above thirty outside Mudmonth is wrong on sight.**

- **The drove** goes up that lane on Thursdays and the count since the second of Mudmonth is floor((day - 2348) / 7) + 1 taken ON OR BEFORE the dateline. **It is 102 at day 3055 and 107 at day 3093, and it went past a hundred in Batch 0002 at day 3041.** The drove paragraph's calendar date is the last Thursday on or before the dateline, **and a writer derives that date from the weekday and not from the count.** Nobody in nine counties has ever watched one go up.
- **The stone** has been carried two miles in one man's own hands since day 2347, elapsed and not inclusive. **It is 708 at day 3055 and 746 at day 3093.**
- **The scar** is counted from day 2580. **It is 475 days old at day 3055 and 513 at day 3093, and it is not cured and it is not going to close over.**
- **The ninth thing**, being the Wethergill end of a cart track, went quiet on the thirteenth of Hearthmonth YR 322, being day 2628, and nobody has been up that track since the second of Goatmonth, being day 2647. **Those two silence figures are counted from two different days and mixing them is the single most likely arithmetic defect in a chapter about that place: the last lime cart was 427 days ago at day 3055 and 465 at day 3093, and the road has been shut 408 days at day 3055 and 446 at day 3093.** Nobody goes up it in this block.
- **The practice mornings** are every day from 2611 to the dateline that is not a Thursday and not a Saturday. **The calendar count is 318 at day 3055 and 345 at day 3093, the count of mornings the practice was due on is 312 and 339, and the loss is six on every one of them.** The practice does not run on the five market mornings of this block's ten datelines and the page says so, **and it does run on the first of Mudmonth at day 3066, which is a Monday and not a market morning.**
- **The number** said out loud at the fourth hour is **four**, it was eight until nine days of water, and it has not gone back, and two of the ten things came back after the water and two have not.
- **The printed notice** was read at the boards on day 2665, the first of Mudmonth was day 2706, it passed with nothing enforced, **and it is three hundred and forty-nine days past its date at day 3055 and three hundred and eighty-seven at day 3093 and has shut nothing.**
- **The roll** was nailed up on day 2827 and is **two hundred and twenty-eight days on the boards at day 3055 and two hundred and sixty-six at day 3093, with nine empty lines on each of three copies and the fourth line empty on all three.** **The sheet on the frame is a fifth thing and stays beside the roll and not over it, and its date is the twenty-ninth of Goatmonth YR 323, being day 3034, being twenty-one days past at day 3055 and fifty-nine days past at day 3093.**
- **The two refusals** of Volume 15 are days 2509 and 2521, and neither man is asked anything.
- **The brood** stands at five frames under about nine straw skirts and no sixth has gone in, and the young man of about nineteen has said out loud three things in that street in about four and a half years and nobody has asked him for an account of them. **Nothing is on the page about the skirts that a character has to act on, and nobody has been asked whether his trade is on one of the nine lines of the hand paper.**
- **The standing broom** is about nine hundred yards of a line nine feet wide and the water laid nearly all of it flat, and it will not close over.
- **The wall's gap** is about nine feet long and four feet high and the ninth yard has not been started, and the mallet is on the bank two miles off with the line of stone and is not picked up. **Four separate things in this county are about nine feet across, being this gap, the width of the made road, the width of the standing broom and the length of that dead line of grass. Carry the noun with the number every time and never print the number on its own.**
- **The four lines of chalk** are on the stone sill of that weigh-house door **under the hood where the rain does not reach**, they mean four, nobody has read them out loud in about four and a half years, and the stick of chalk is in a press drawer and the man of about fifty-four has not asked for it.
- **The leaf at the back of that day-book carries nine figures and a date and the names of nobody**, and the day-book stands at eleven entries and the register holds ten questions with no finding under any of them.
- **The bleed** began on the fifth of Wolfmonth YR 323, being day 2920, and is **one hundred and thirty-five days old at day 3055 and one hundred and seventy-three at day 3093, and it has not faded and nobody in nine counties knows about it and it is in no document and it gets no panel.**
- **The hand lamp** goes on the coping at the low side of that causeway four days south every Monday afternoon in the winter, **and three of this block's ten datelines are Mondays, being 3059, 3066 and 3087, so a writer may put the lamp there on the afternoon of any one of those three and may not put it there on any of the other seven, and the page says the afternoon is the lamp's if it says it at all.**
- **The firsts of a month** are twenty-sixth at day 3066 and that one carries Chapter 0822, **and the count is not begun again.** The next two are twenty-seventh at day 3126 and twenty-eighth at day 3156, and both are outside this block.
- **THE FIRST OF A MONTH WITH THE PRACTICE RUNNING ON IT IS AVAILABLE IN THIS BLOCK AND NOT IN THE LAST TWO, being that day 3066 is a Monday, and a writer who wants that beat takes 3066 and does not go looking for it elsewhere.**
